title: SSB Interview Preparation 2026: 5-Day Process and Tips
metaDescription: SSB interview preparation 2026: the 5-day process, screening, psychology tests and GTO tasks. The 15 officer-like qualities and how to prepare.
headline: SSB Interview Preparation 2026: The 5-Day Process, Tests and Tips

sections.title: What is the SSB interview?
sections.content:
The Services Selection Board interview is a five-day personality and intelligence assessment that decides who receives a commission in the Indian Army, Navy or Air Force. It is the single gate between clearing a written exam such as NDA, CDS, AFCAT, TES or NCC Special Entry and becoming an officer, and it has been used in its modern form since the late 1940s.

Three assessors judge you independently: the Interviewing Officer, the Group Testing Officer and the Psychologist. They grade you on 15 officer-like qualities, and all three must recommend you for selection. There is no syllabus to memorise; the five days are simply different windows into the same person.

sections.title: Day 1: screening — OIR and PPDT
sections.content:
Day 1 begins with reporting and document verification, followed by the Officer Intelligence Rating test, a verbal and non-verbal reasoning paper, and the Picture Perception and Description Test. In the PPDT you are shown a hazy picture for 30 seconds, write a story, narrate it to your group and discuss it together.

Roughly 50 to 60 percent of candidates are screened out on the evening of Day 1 and sent home, so this is the sharpest cut in the whole process. The way through is a clear, positive story with a resolute hero, confident narration and active listening in the group discussion, not domination of it.

sections.title: Day 2: psychology tests — TAT, WAT, SRT, SDT
sections.content:
Day 2 is the psychology battery, run by the Psychologist. The Thematic Apperception Test asks for 12 stories from pictures plus one blank slide, the Word Association Test gives 60 words at 15 seconds each, the Situation Reaction Test gives 60 situations in 30 minutes, and the Self Description asks for five short essays about yourself.

There are no right or wrong answers, only officer-like and un-officer-like ones. The winning approach is honest, consistent and positive: stories with a hero who faces problems and solves them, quick first responses in WAT, and practical, decisive answers in SRT that match the person you show in the interview.

sections.title: Days 3–5: GTO tasks, interview and conference
sections.content:
Days 3 and 4 belong to the Group Testing Officer, with nine tasks across the two days: group discussion, group planning exercise, progressive group task, half group task, lecturette, individual obstacles, command task, final group task and the snake race. The personal interview by the Interviewing Officer is staggered across days 2 to 4 and usually lasts 45 to 60 minutes.

Day 5 is the conference: the full board, including the President and Deputy President, meets each candidate for a few minutes and then deliberates and announces the result. Prepare with daily fitness, current affairs for discussions and the lecturette, deep knowledge of your own life story, and mock SSB sessions so the format feels familiar before you report.

faqs.q: How long is the SSB interview and what are the stages?
faqs.a: The SSB interview runs for five days. Day 1 is screening with the Officer Intelligence Rating test and the Picture Perception test, and half the candidates are sent home. Day 2 covers psychology tests, days 3 and 4 cover group testing tasks and the personal interview, and day 5 is the final conference where the board announces who is recommended.

faqs.q: What are the 15 officer-like qualities in SSB?
faqs.a: The 15 officer-like qualities are effective intelligence, reasoning ability, organising ability, power of expression, social adaptability, cooperation, sense of responsibility, initiative, self-confidence, speed of decision, ability to influence the group, liveliness, determination, courage and stamina. Three assessors judge these qualities independently through different tests, and all three must recommend you for selection.

faqs.q: Is there a fixed passing mark in the SSB interview?
faqs.a: No, there is no fixed passing mark in the SSB interview. Candidates are assessed on the 15 officer-like qualities by three independent assessors: the interviewing officer, the group testing officer and the psychologist. All three must recommend a candidate for selection, and the final decision is taken together in the day 5 conference.

faqs.q: How should I prepare for the SSB interview?
faqs.a: Prepare across all three sides of the assessment: mind, speech and action. Practise OIR reasoning and picture stories under time pressure, and write honest WAT and SRT responses daily. Build fitness for the GTO ground tasks, stay updated on current affairs for group discussions, and know your own life story deeply for the interview.
